thread:
mia: Hey team — getting an on-call alert: sudden spike of 401s from edge workers and huge retries causing a billing spike for a few customers. Suspect packaging/bundler issue with the Node/Edge SDK bundle. Anyone seen this pattern? :eyes:

infra-bot: alert: 2026-03-16 14:12Z - 401 rate increased 1200% for org 'acme-io' across eu-west-1 edge routes. Retry count per request ~ 7.

devon: Can you paste minimal repro + which SDK version? Also, edge vs node runtime?

mia: SDK @redwood/sdk-js v0.9.3. Customer using Next.js edge middleware + pnpm v8, turbopack for builds. Repro repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/support-repro-exports-shadow (private). Quick log:
```
fetch "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"  -> 401 responses
client retry loop: 401 -> retry -> 401 -> retry x7
Authorization header not present on actual outbound request from edge runtime
```

samir: Authorization missing usually means bundler replaced the Node entry with a browser/edge shim that intentionally drops headers (for browsers). Could be our exports map resolving wrong subpath for edge builds. Do you have package.json from the customer bundle?

mia: Got the package.json they shipped (part):
```
"exports": {
  "./package.json": "./package.json",
  "./*": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/$1.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/$1.js",
    "browser": "./dist/edge/$1.js"
  }
}
```
Note: they use deep imports like `@redwood/sdk-js/lib/client` in code. bundler resolved `./lib/client` -> `./dist/edge/lib/client.js` (browser/edge build) which intentionally wraps fetch to drop Authorization in certain runtimes for security. That caused the client to attempt auth-less calls and trigger retries (and billing).

jess: Oof. So two issues: 1) our exports map with `./*` + `browser` is being preferred by bundlers for serverless edge builds; 2) retries are configured globally and treat 401 as retryable by default.

devon: Can you share a small repro command we can run locally to mimic customer's build?

mia: Steps i used locally:
1) clone repro 
2) pnpm install --shamefully-hoist (their monorepo setup)
3) pnpm build (next build with turbopack)
4) run `node ./scripts/trace-fetch.js` in a simulated edge env (node 18 with undici)
Trace shows: `Outbound fetch headers: {}` instead of `{ authorization: 'Bearer ...' }`.

samir: Quick debug: run `node -e "console.log(require('./node_modules/@redwood/sdk-js/package.json').exports)"` inside their repo to see resolution. Also dump the bundle with `pnpm dlx why @redwood/sdk-js` and inspect resolved file.

mia: Did that — shows resolved to `dist/edge/lib/client.js`.

ai-support: Note: customers using server-side edge runtimes (Next.js Edge) should prefer our explicit `edge` entrypoint, but not one that strips headers. We used a different wrapper for browser consumers (to avoid leaking secrets), but the bundler is collapsing browser & edge.

devon: Actionable short-term mitigations?

samir: Workarounds for customers:
- Pin to `@redwood/sdk-js@0.9.2` where exports map didn't include the `browser` field for deep subpaths (if that helps).
- Force bundler alias to point to `@redwood/sdk-js/dist/cjs/lib/client.js` (or the Node entry) in next.config.js: `webpack: {resolve: {alias: {'@redwood/sdk-js': path.resolve(__dirname, 'node_modules/@redwood/sdk-js/dist/cjs/index.js')}}}` or equivalent for turbopack.
- As immediate server workaround, disable automatic retries for 401s in client config: `new RedwoodClient({ retry: { onStatus: (s)=> s !== 401 } })` — not ideal but stops billing loop.

jess: For the platform: we need to release a patch to exports map so bundlers don't accidentally pick browser shim for server edge runtimes. Also update docs warning about deep imports.

mia: I've opened support ticket & asking finance for temporary credits for impacted orgs. Also filed a mini PR with a suggested exports change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/204 (draft).

samir: Proposed exports tweak (idea): explicitly enumerate deep subpaths and avoid `browser` fallback for `./*` so server resolvers prefer `require`/`import` entries. Example snippet: 
```
"exports": {
  "./package.json": "./package.json",
  "./index": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" },
  "./lib/*": { "import": "./dist/esm/lib/$1.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/lib/$1.js" }
}
```
This avoids `browser` at the glob level.

devon: Good. Also add integration test: build with pnpm/turbopack/vite and verify header passthrough for server-edge bundles. Add a CI step to catch accidental browser resolution for server-side builds.

mia: Customer applied temporary alias and turned off 401 retries; errors dropped to normal and billing stabilized. Finance asked for list of impacted requests to evaluate credits.

jess: Next steps assigned: 
- samir: patch exports + open release (v0.9.4) and add CI test (ETA 2 business days).
- devon: write KB article for support + recommended bundler workarounds (ETA EOD).
- mia: collect impacted request IDs & submit finance request (ETA today).

devon: I'll also add an SDK config flag to make 401 non-retryable by default for edge runtimes in next minor if we decide it's safe.

mia: Thanks all. Keeping thread updated. :heart:
